[b]Two Thousand Meters Underwater[/b]

"Like being inside a spacesuit, but on the wrong side of the world." That's how renowned diver Shen Congxu described the feeling when he made this same dive into Qianxun Major on the 3rd of April, 2006. It's been two decades since then, and little has changed down here, in the world beneath the world. 

The three divers stared at the bottom hatch as it swung inward. But no deluge flooded in. Instead, the water all around the bell stilled, held at bay by the immense internal pressure, forming up into a perfectly calm meniscus just below the hatchway. 

"People call this the moonpool, pretty ain't it?" Kang muttered over the comms. "But no staring for too long, it's time to study the world. Everyone, state your name, some nice words, and then drop in, gentlemen."

"Wei Jie," said the first and eldest of the three aquanauts, his voice a gruff and fatherly timbre. "Team leader of the [i]Hai Xia[/i], reporting here on the 11th of December, 2025. I am very nervous but excited to go. With good help from Comrade Kang, I hope we accomplish all of our set goals and return home safe and sound."

"My name is Lin Tao." The second says, crackling with excitement. "As Comrade Wei has said, let us hope to find something nice."

"Xu Hai." The last aquanaut murmurs, and then no more.

After one final check of their suits, the three divers descended into the mirror. The transition was instantaneous. One moment, they were in the dry, brightly lit, shriekingly loud chamber of the bell. Next, they were suspended in a silence so imperious and absolute, like perceptible and physical darkness itself, enveloping them in a frigid hug, broken up only by the beams of their suit lights and of the bell from whence they came. Their umbilicals, now connected to the bell's internal systems, paid out behind them like synthetic roots.

"Water overcomes fire." Kang Hongxin reminded the three divers as their suits settled into the rocky bottom of the lake floor. His voice was devoid of awe or fear. "Remember that death surrounds you, and you will survive. Act foolishly, and you will not."

The aquanauts dared not challenge Kang's firm orders.

"Good. Move out together to the first sonar ping. If it's a cave system, move slowly and carefully and always keep your lines visible to one another. If silt starts to kick up, pull out as quickly as you can without damaging your suits.

As if on cue, a quiet ringing sound would start bouncing back to them. It was sonar from the [i]Hai Xia[/i], which had begun targeting one of several objects of interest that Kang had been researching over these past few years. The aquanauts gave each other a quick nod and then moved out. Wei led the group carefully through the freezing darkness. As Kang had warned, their metal feet sank into the soft, oozing silt, kicking up clouds of fine sediment that hung in the water like fog. The world was reduced to the three cones of light and the eerie, squeaky sound of their own breathing. Strange, pallid creaturesblind, white crabs, sinuous worms that retreated into tubesscuttled away from the alien light, creatures for whom the concept of a sun was a biological impossibility.

They walked for what felt like an eternity, the sonar ping growing stronger in their headphones, like a quiet drummer boy, beating more and more frantically in the approach to the final crescendo. Then, silence. The three aquanauts ventured into the first cave system, but stopped after only a few seconds. There was nothing there; the cave couldn't even be properly called a cave. It was shallow, more akin to a superficial scar embedded in the lakebed. Kang then directed them to a second cave. Then a third. A fourth.

An aqunaut was to serve a saturation diving mission for up to a full month, but each actual "run" in the deep waters only really lasted up to six hours. There was only so much that the atmospheric diving suit could protect you from, against the bitter cold, the sheer weight of their own suits, dehydration and exhaustion, never mind mental fatigue. Then there were the dives themselves. The first cave came shallow, but all succeeding ones were great and deep and labyrinthine that cradled the aquanauts in a blanket of deep darkness. 

In the heart of the void were only two comforts: The light emanated from your ADS, and the safety of your fellow aquanauts, who seemed more and more distant as you traversed the claustrophobic gaps of the basalt and mudstone.

Aquanauts typically labored for six hours, but they had been caving for eight. After the fifth cave complex was investigated, the exhausted aquanauts were ordered back up into the bell to take their rest. By then, even the joyous walk back to the bell with its beds and hot meals seemed so distant and horrible, and the younger aquanaut Lin had to be physically dragged up to his feet by Wei and Xu.

"You overwork us, Comrade Kang!" Wei jokingly accused into his headpiece, raising himself up from the moonpool and into the bell, his voice interspersing between jubilation and exhaustion.  "Will we be made Heroes of Labor? Haha!"

"Heh. Apologies, comrades, it won't happen again." Kang replied. "The first warm-up session is always longest. I shall obey our labor laws in the succeeding ones, so get some good rest!"

"You could've killed us." Xu Hai quietly mentioned, slumping against one of the bell walls, clearly nonplussed by this trial by water.

"Water overcomes fire, Comrade Xu," Kang said, his voice mildly soured by Xu's interjection, yet nevertheless affable. "You were all surrounded by darkness, silt, and two thousand meters of water over. You should expect to be killed at any moment. You may be exhausted today, but you will be less so tomorrow, and better after. By the end of this month, the labors that nearly killed you today will have become meaningless trivialities."

"Don't mind Comrade Xu, he's just not used to these sorts of things, same as I! We can't all be accepting of danger after all!" Wei interjected, helping the trembling Lin and indignant Xu to seal the bell hatch shut. 

Once the bell had been closed off, the three men sat together in silence for a moment as Kang provided them with a brief overview of their own findings, the mistakes that had been made during the eight-hour journey, and what they should expect tomorrow. Then, he signed off. The three men waited at their respective seats as the bell slowly began to raise them back up and into shallower waters. Normally, this rapid rise would kill a diver, but the bell remained tightly pressurized, preventing the dissolved gases in their bodies from erupting into fatal bubbles. Darkness turned to light, black to gorgeous blue, and the unfamiliar world of the abyss was supplanted by familiar carps, breams, and eels.

Then, they were out of the water.

The bell raised itself up and out of the Qianxun Major and carefully fused back into the side of the [i]Hai Xia[/i], a small hissing sound permeating through the air. It was the sound of the bell and the hyperbaric chamber of the ship finally merging back into one. A bright green light illuminated at the side of the bell, and the side hatch opened. Out of the claustrophobic bell, the three aquanauts waddled back onto the hyperbaric chamber, twisting and contorting their bodies into unseemly postures to rid themselves of the heavy ADS they'd been wearing all this time, their bodies slick with sweat and the all-consuming smell of the lake.

Kang, watching the three men emerge from the bell, waved at them, his mouth slowly creasing into a wide grin.

"All in one piece, it looks like!" He jested, and the men laughed.
